text:
Lia (Sales): Quick POC question from ACME — they want EU-only data residency for the trial. Can we confirm whether hosted API guarantees EU residency, and if not what's the recommended path? Also they need the current sub‑processor list and the routing/fallback behavior if eu capacity is saturated.

Evan (Solutions Eng): Short answer: hosted API does not guarantee physical EU-only processing for every request today; we do region preference but capacity/fallbacks may route to compatible variants. For strict residency you can use Dedicated (reserved) or Private (VPC/on-prem).

Lia (Sales): Got it — customer is okay with a short-term POC but legal asked for a sub-processor list and an explicit routing policy statement for the contract. Can we produce that ASAP? :pray:

Anna (Security): I can share the sub-processor list and DPA text. We have a standard EU subproc list for hosted regions. I'll attach the document to the ticket, but here's the public summary: data at rest + inference tokens processed in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 where available; sub-processors: AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1) for backups, Datadog (metrics), Sentry (errors). Full list via internal link.

Mike (Infra): Routing details: by default our router uses region_preference + model_compatibility heuristics. If eu pools are full we try burst capacity in same cloud region, then fallback to dedicated pools in other regions configured for the customer. For POC we can set a strict policy to pin to eu-only until they sign a residency commitment.

Evan (Solutions Eng): If you want a statement for legal, use this language (copy/paste): "For the POC, Redwood will enforce EU-only processing by pinning requests to eu-region capacity. If no eu-region capacity is available, requests will be rejected until capacity is restored or an explicit exception is granted in writing." That maps to our routing flag enforce_residency: true.

Mike (Infra): Config snippet we can apply to the POC tenant (ops runs this):

```yaml
routing_policy:
  region_preference: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]
  enforce_residency: true
  fallback: reject
```

Evan (Solutions Eng): Note: fallback: reject will surface 503s if eu capacity is exhausted — good for legal proof but may make the POC flaky. Alternative is fallback: dedicated (requires reserved capacity) or fallback: queue (delayed processing).

Lia (Sales): Customer will accept temporary 503s for strict residency during POC. Can we get subproc list + the legal language and that config applied this week? Timeline: demo Wed.

Anna (Security): I'll upload the subproc CSV and a signed DPA template to the Salesforce opportunity and ping legal. Link to internal doc: https://redwood.internal/security/subprocessors/eu

DeployBot: [ops] Tenant pointer oc-acme-poc queued for routing_policy update by @mike

Mike (Infra): I'll schedule the change for Tue 18:00 UTC, will confirm once applied. @Lia please put the customer IP ranges if they want IP allowlist for the private control plane.

Lia (Sales): Thanks team — putting IPs in the ticket now. Will update ACME. :thumbsup:
